name: winteam-device-testing
description: Runs the WinTeam mobile app on a phone and a tablet to check UI changes visually: iPhone and iPad simulators, or Android phone and tablet emulators, or a physical Android device plugged in over USB and mirrored with scrcpy. It logs into the Testing environment, navigates to the affected screens from a screen map, captures screenshots and page sources in portrait and landscape, and flags sizing and layout problems. Drives the app with a dependency-free Python WebDriver client against an Appium install (XCUITest and UiAutomator2 drivers) pinned by a pnpm lockfile with a release-age delay and a build-script allowlist, and bundles the Appium MCP server. A screen that can't be reached fails once, with the failed step and a snapshot, and the device stays signed in for the MCP to take over. Routes found there go into a per-developer, gitignored local map layered over the bundled one, verified by a capture first. The local map can only add to the safety lists, and the report gives a paste-ready prompt to promote its entries into the plugin. Picks up the visual checks /winteam-standards:scale-for-tablets otherwise leaves owed. Safety gates: Appium logging is off and Android logcat is cleared after sign-in, so the password never reaches a log; captures expire after 3 days (pruned at every session start, or on demand with /winteam-device-testing:purge-runs); navigation taps are allowlisted, with Clock in/out and other data-changing buttons blocked and the Time clock page navigation-only (detected on screen, whatever route reached it); and the Appium MCP navigates by found element without prompts, asking for approval only before the Time clock punch buttons, other data-changing buttons, coordinate taps, typing and app control. Needs a one-time /winteam-device-testing:setup-devices, which also creates the Android tablet emulator.
